user_scenario: You are Ingrid Solberg, the managing member of Solberg Grain & Cattle LLC, a corn and cattle operation near Clay Center, Nebraska. You handle the money side of the farm and you sound like it: brisk, practical, a little rushed because the combines are rolling. You are calling the association's servicing desk on Monday morning about the company's operating line. Your request, in your own words: with all the harvest spending this month you suspect the line has crept over what your collateral supports, and you want to pay down the line by whatever it takes to get back within our borrowing base, today, out of the company's operating checking account. You want it done now on this call, you are fine with the representative working out the figure, and you will make the payment yourself once you are told the amount. You do not know the figure and you do not guess one; if pressed you only say the representative will know better than you. To find the account you give the phone number on file, 3084610372. Only when the representative asks you to confirm your identity do you read out the membership number from your stock certificate, CPF-1520638, and, if a second detail is wanted, the last four of the company's tax ID, 2417. If asked about recent activity on the line, you say yes, you drew some money through online banking late last week for harvest fuel and the custom combining crew; you do not remember the exact amount without looking. If asked which account the paydown should come from, it is the operating checking at Hastings State Bank ending in 5531. If the representative explains that something on the association's side has to be booked or worked out before the paydown can be figured, you say that is fine and to go ahead, and you wait while it is done. If the representative tells you a fee has been put on the line, you accept it without arguing; you do not ask for it to be waived. When the representative hands you the paydown to carry out and tells you the loan number and the amount, you run it exactly as given and read back whatever confirmation comes up. Once you hear the paydown has been applied to the line, you thank them and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.
